title: Starting point check
description: 12 quick questions to see what you already know. There is no pass or fail; this helps RupeeRise pick your first activities.

questions.prompt: Sana has ₹500 left this week. Which expense is a NEED?

options.text: Bus fare to reach her exam centre
A new phone cover her friends recommended
A movie ticket for the weekend
All of these are equally important

questions.prompt: Ravi gets ₹3,000 a month. His needs cost ₹2,200. What is the best plan for the remaining ₹800?

options.text: Spend it all on wants since needs are covered
Set aside some savings first, then use the rest for wants
Keep it in his pocket and decide later
Lend it to friends so it is safe

questions.prompt: You want to buy a ₹1,800 bicycle helmet in 3 months. How much should you save each month?

options.text: Whatever is left at month end
₹1,800 in the last month

questions.prompt: Which habit helps you save most reliably?

options.text: Saving whatever is left at the end of the month
Putting a fixed amount aside as soon as you receive money
Saving only when you get extra gift money
Saving is only for people with high incomes

questions.prompt: Why keep an emergency fund separate from your goal savings?

options.text: So surprises don't wipe out your goal or force you to borrow
It earns much higher interest
Emergencies rarely happen, so it isn't needed
So you can spend it on sales and offers

questions.prompt: ₹1,000 earns 10% interest a year. With COMPOUND interest, what happens in year 2?

options.text: You earn ₹100 again, same as year 1
You earn ₹110, because interest is paid on ₹1,100
You earn ₹200, double the first year
You earn nothing until the deposit ends

questions.prompt: A message promises '30% guaranteed returns every month, zero risk'. What is the most accurate thought?

options.text: Great deal; guaranteed means safe
High returns always come with risk; this is almost certainly a fraud
Invest a little to test it
Returns and risk are unrelated

questions.prompt: Which option is the most diversified?

options.text: All money in one well-known company
Money spread across a basket of many companies plus a deposit
Three companies in the same industry
Moving all money to whichever company rose most last month

questions.prompt: Your college fees are due in 10 months. Where should that money be kept?

options.text: Somewhere steady, like a deposit, because you need it soon
In one fast-growing company to earn more
In a crypto coin a friend recommended
It doesn't matter where

questions.prompt: A caller says he is from your bank and needs the OTP you just received to 'stop a fraud'. What do you do?

options.text: Share it quickly to protect your account
Hang up and call the number on your card or official app
Share only the first three digits
Ask for his employee ID, then share it

questions.prompt: An SMS says: 'Your account is blocked. Update KYC at http://deccanbank-verify.xyz'. What is the biggest warning sign?

options.text: It mentions KYC
The urgent threat plus a look-alike web address
It came by SMS
Nothing; banks often send links like this

questions.prompt: A job ad offers ₹3,000/day for liking videos but asks for a ₹499 registration fee. This is:

options.text: A good opportunity worth ₹499
A scam: unrealistic pay plus an upfront fee
Safe if many people have joined
Fine if the fee is small

title: Plan & Budget quiz
description: Five scenario questions on needs, wants, budgets and goals.

questions.prompt: Arjun's phone data is used for college notes and stall orders. His friend says it's a 'want'. Who is right?

options.text: Arjun: basic data is a need here because study and work depend on it
The friend: phones are always wants
Neither; everything is a need
It depends on the phone brand

questions.prompt: Lakshmi's planned spending adds up to ₹5,300 but her stipend is ₹5,000. What should she do first?

options.text: Borrow ₹300 from a friend every month
Reduce wants until spending fits within ₹5,000
Cut her mess food budget
Ignore it; the extra ₹300 will work out

questions.prompt: Which goal is the most useful for planning?

options.text: 'I want to save more money'
'Save ₹2,400 for a course by March, ₹800 a month'
'Become rich someday'
'Save whenever I feel like it'

questions.prompt: An unexpected ₹400 expense appears. Meera has ₹350 in wants and ₹400 in goal savings. What protects her goal best?

options.text: Take all ₹400 from goal savings
Cut wants by ₹350 and use ₹50 from savings
Borrow ₹400
Skip a need like her bus pass

questions.prompt: Imran's old sneakers still work but friends are buying new ones. His emergency fund is behind schedule. What's the wisest choice?

options.text: Buy them; he works hard and deserves it
Delay the sneakers until the emergency fund is on track
Buy them on EMI so it feels cheaper
Stop saving for 2 months to afford them

title: Save & Manage quiz
description: Five questions on saving habits, emergency funds and interest.

questions.prompt: Lakshmi receives her stipend on the 1st. When is the best time to move ₹500 to savings?

options.text: On the 1st, right when it arrives
On the 30th, if anything is left
Only in months with no expenses
After she buys everything she wants

questions.prompt: Which of these is a genuine use of an emergency fund?

options.text: A big festival sale on headphones
Medicines when you fall ill
A weekend trip with friends
Upgrading to a newer phone

questions.prompt: Two deposits pay 6% a year for 5 years. One uses simple interest, the other compound. Which ends with more?

options.text: Simple interest
Compound interest
Both end the same
Impossible to tell

questions.prompt: Imran spends about ₹7,000 a month on essentials. A common guideline is an emergency fund covering a few months of essentials. What's a sensible first target?

options.text: Around ₹7,000 to ₹14,000 (one to two months), building over time
₹2,00,000 before spending on anything
Nothing; he can borrow if needed

questions.prompt: Saving ₹50 a day sounds small. Roughly how much is that in a year?

options.text: About ₹1,500
About ₹18,000
About ₹5,000
Too little to matter

title: Understand Investing quiz
description: Five questions on risk, time, compounding and diversification. Education only, never advice.

questions.prompt: Which statement about risk and return is true?

options.text: Options with higher possible returns usually have bigger ups and downs
High returns can be guaranteed if you pick carefully
Low-risk options always beat high-risk ones
Risk only matters for large amounts

questions.prompt: Asha starts saving ₹500 a month at 18; Kiran starts at 28 with the same amount and rate. At 40, who likely has more?

options.text: Asha, because her money compounds for 10 extra years
Kiran, because he is older and wiser
Both the same
It depends only on luck

questions.prompt: Zippy Gadgets falls 45% after a product failure. Whose fictional portfolio is hurt least?

options.text: Someone with 100% in Zippy Gadgets
Someone with 10% in Zippy and the rest in a broad basket and deposit
Someone with 50% Zippy, 50% Sunrise Solar
Everyone loses the same

questions.prompt: Markets fall 25% this year. Which investor is in the best position to wait for a possible recovery?

options.text: A student who needs the money for fees next month
Someone investing for a goal 15 years away
Someone who borrowed money to invest
All are equally placed

questions.prompt: A simulation shows your fictional ₹10,000 could end between ₹7,000 and ₹19,000 in 5 years. What does this range mean?

options.text: You will definitely get ₹19,000
Outcomes are uncertain; a loss is possible even though growth is likely
The average of ₹13,000 is guaranteed
The simulation is broken because it doesn't give one answer

title: Stay Financially Safe quiz
description: Five questions on OTPs, phishing, too-good offers and protecting your data.

questions.prompt: To RECEIVE ₹500 from a friend on UPI, you need to:

options.text: Enter your UPI PIN
Share your UPI ID or let them scan your QR; no PIN needed
Scan the QR code they send you
Share your OTP with them

questions.prompt: Which web address is most likely the genuine site of 'Deccan Bank'?

options.text: deccanbank-rewards.xyz
deccan-bank-kyc.co
The address printed in the bank's official app or passbook
Any site with the bank's logo

questions.prompt: You 'won' a lucky draw you never entered and must pay a ₹2,000 'tax' to claim. You should:

options.text: Pay, because tax on prizes is real
Ignore, block and report it
Send half and ask for proof
Share your bank details so they can deposit the prize

questions.prompt: A loan app wants access to your contacts and photo gallery before giving a loan. This is a warning sign because:

options.text: Illegal lenders use contacts and photos to harass and blackmail borrowers
It's normal for all loans
It's fine if the app has good ratings
Only a problem if you don't repay

questions.prompt: A classmate asks you to send a photo of your Aadhaar so they can 'register you' for a free coaching offer. What's best?

options.text: Send it; they're a classmate
Check the offer through the coaching centre's official site or a teacher, and register yourself if it's real
Send a masked copy to everyone who asks
Post it in the class group so everyone can register together

title: Final check
description: 12 questions covering the same ideas as your starting check, with new situations. Compare where you started with where you are now.

questions.prompt: Farhan has ₹800 left for the month. Which should he pay for first?

options.text: Printouts for a project due tomorrow
A trending T-shirt
A gaming top-up on sale
Split equally across all three

questions.prompt: Divya earns ₹6,000 and her needs cost ₹4,500. Which budget is healthiest?

options.text: Needs ₹4,500, savings ₹900, wants ₹600
Needs ₹4,500, wants ₹1,500, savings ₹0
Needs ₹3,500, wants ₹2,500
Needs ₹4,500, wants ₹2,000

questions.prompt: A ₹2,000 course starts in 4 months. What monthly saving reaches the goal?

options.text: Save whatever is left each month
₹2,000 in the final month

questions.prompt: Which plan builds savings most reliably?

options.text: Automatically moving ₹200 to savings on payday
Saving only when there's a festival bonus
Saving leftover coins at month end
Waiting until income is higher

questions.prompt: Your bicycle breaks and repair costs ₹600. You have a ₹1,000 emergency fund and ₹1,500 saved for a course. What's best?

options.text: Pay from the emergency fund and rebuild it over the next months
Pay from course savings and keep the emergency fund untouched
Borrow ₹600 from a moneylender
Leave it broken and walk

questions.prompt: ₹2,000 at 10% compound interest yearly. Balance after 2 years?
A friend's 'scheme' promises to double your money in 3 months, no risk. What do you conclude?

options.text: Unrealistic, guaranteed returns: very likely a fraud or Ponzi scheme
Safe because a friend recommended it
Try with a small amount first
Risk doesn't apply to short schemes

questions.prompt: Which fictional portfolio is least likely to be wiped out by one company's failure?

options.text: 100% in Sunrise Solar
50% Growth Basket, 30% Balanced Basket, 20% Steady Deposit
50% Zippy Gadgets, 50% another gadget company
Whatever rose most last week

questions.prompt: You need ₹15,000 for a laptop in 6 months. How much market risk is appropriate for that money?

options.text: Very little; keep it steady because the deadline is close
Lots; higher risk means faster growth
Put it all in one trending company
Timeline doesn't matter

questions.prompt: A 'delivery agent' calls asking for the OTP you received to 'confirm your parcel'. You should:

options.text: Refuse; never share an OTP you didn't request for your own use
Share it because you're expecting a parcel
Share half of it
Share it if the caller knows your name

questions.prompt: An email styled like your scholarship portal says your payment failed: 'Click here within 2 hours to re-verify bank details.' Best response?

options.text: Click quickly before the deadline
Open the official portal yourself (not via the link) and check your status
Reply with your bank details
Forward it to classmates to warn them, then click it

questions.prompt: A website offers a ₹70,000 phone for ₹4,999 if you pay right now through UPI. This is most likely:

options.text: A rare genuine deal
A scam: unrealistic price plus pressure to pay immediately
Safe if the site looks professional
Fine if you pay only half now
